messages:
alex: incident-bot just paged me, GPU queue spike across us-west-2 cluster. latency alerts + 5min sustained queue growth. anyone oncall?
incident-bot: Paging sre-oncall (severity: P1) — GPU queue length > 1200 for 5m, throttling rate > 30%
sre-oncall: I'm on it. grabbing metrics, can someone post what pools are affected?
maria: seeing 80% of requests hitting the inference:gpu-prod pool, backlog building on pool-gpu-ml-03 and pool-gpu-ml-04. autoscaler shows pending nodes but they never register.
tariq: logs from autoscaler: "ProvisionTimeout: nodes stuck in CNI_ATTACH" and then repeated API 409s when trying to bind volumes. guess infra quota or cloud provider flaps.
alex: also getting runtime driver Xid 13 packets — nodes reporting multiple CUDA/Xid errors before disappearing. suspect driver instability + node hotplug.
maria: checked node histories — several nodes had kernel oopses and the nvidia module reloaded around the same time (~3032109600). after reload GPUs went into 'unavailable' state until driver restart.
sre-oncall: root cause hypothesis: recent kernel module update combined with hotplug events causing devices to detach intermittently -> effective GPU capacity dropped and autoscaler kept trying to add nodes but provisioning hung due to volume attach race.
customer-success-sam: have we confirmed customer impact? one large customer (acme-inc) reported multi-second stalls in logs and increased 5xxs. CS is prepping a notification.
tariq: posting snippet of autoscaler log: ```ERROR autoscaler: failed to register node: AttachVolume failed: APIError 409: volume busy
INFO autoscaler: retrying provision in 30s
```
maria: and driver logs: ```NVRM: Xid (PCIe) 13 detected at GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus
kernel: nvidia 0000:03:00.0: GPU unplugged
```
alex: mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler to stop noisy provisioning 2) cordon suspect nodes 3) add temporary capacity in warm pool (if available) 4) enable CPU-fallback routing for low-priority tenants 5) schedule driver rolling restart with specific kernel module flags.
sre-oncall: taking steps now. pausing autoscaler; setting policy paused=true.
tariq: paused. I'm increasing warm pool min count by 10 in us-west-2 to try to buy headroom. cloud console shows 6 warm nodes starting.
maria: I'm cordoning and draining nodes that show repeated Xid/ooms: gpu-node-12, gpu-node-19, gpu-node-27. doing safe evictions for in-flight sessions.
incident-bot: deploy-bot started a canary of a small restart on gpu-node-31 (driver reload with --no-guc). Logs streamed to /var/log/driver-restart.
alex: can we route non-critical inference to CPU-only fallback for next 30m? lower-cost customers OK. This should reduce queue pressure while we repair GPUs.
customer-success-sam: confirm ACME is in the high-priority pool; they need SLA contact. I've opened a private channel with their SRE and drafting a short update: "We are investigating elevated latency due to GPU node instability; routing fallback where possible; will update every 30 minutes."
maria: quick note — the autoscaler UI still shows "pending" for 12 nodes stuck in attach. I'm hitting cloud API and see vpc ENI attach rate limits. raising support ticket with cloud provider.
tariq: workaround: switched attach policy to use secondary subnets to spread ENI attach across AZs. that freed 3 nodes which now registered.
sre-oncall: registered nodes increased by 4 -> queue reduced ~40% in last 8m. throughput back up but still throttling.
alex: why did driver reload cause unplug? any config we changed recently? we pushed a packaging update last week that touched driver packaging on some images.
maria: yes, kernel-driver mismatch on a small subset. We're rolling a revert to the package on the problematic AMI set and will force-reboot those nodes after drain.
incident-bot: severity remains P1. next status update in 15m.
tariq: patch applied to AMI set boot-2026-03-10 -> rolling replace starting. reboots going out slowly to avoid mass outage.
maria: manual mitigation for queue: increased inference route weight to models on cpu-fallback group (weights adjusted) and enabled transient caching for common prompts to reduce token regen.
alex: customer impact summary for initial page: ~2% requests experienced 5xxs, 18% increased latency >2s, peak queue depth 1300. impacted customers: ACME (critical), beta-testers (medium), general free tier (minor).
customer-success-sam: sent customer update at 21:12 UTC, included mitigation steps and ETA for next update. ACME response: appreciate the update, please prioritize ACME routing to remaining healthy GPUs.
sre-oncall: created follow-up ticket referencing cloud support SR-8932 for ENI rate limits; assigned to infra team.
maria: completed AMI rollback on two AZs, 7 nodes replaced and registered successfully. driver Xid noise dropped significantly.
tariq: autoscaler resumed with conservative scaling policy (maxScale 30% more than baseline) to avoid thrash.
incident-bot: autoscaler resumed at 21:45 UTC. monitoring for 30m.
alex: still seeing one node (gpu-node-44) flapping; I've isolated it and will decommission later. for now it's cordoned and out of rotation.
customer-success-sam: ACME confirmed reduction in errors, they requested a post-incident RCA. I'll coordinate with triage.
sre-oncall: summary of mitigations: paused autoscaler -> cordon/drain bad nodes -> AMI rollback and driver reload -> switched ENI attach subnets -> increased warm pool -> CPU-fallback routing -> resumed autoscaler with conservative limits.
maria: recommended long-term fixes: (1) harden driver packaging in AMI pipeline, (2) add grace backoff on autoscaler for ENI attach 409s, (3) add health-check gating before marking node as available, (4) telemetry on Xid spikes to trigger automated quarantine.
tariq: created tickets for each recommendation and tagged infra + runtime teams.
alex: thanks everyone. we'll keep monitoring for 60m and prepare an RCA draft once we collect more logs. closing the live mitigation thread, will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
